name: Carrion Defense Works Necrotizing Agent Sprayer NAS-2 'Rot'
description: A handheld sprayer that disperses a fast-acting necrotizing agent — Carrion's proprietary NecroSolve compound — that causes rapid enzymatic breakdown of biological tissue on contact. The compound is highly selective for living tissue and has no effect on synthetic materials, making it particularly horrifying: it eats flesh but leaves clothing, cyberware, and equipment untouched. A 2-second exposure to the spray causes surface tissue necrosis across the contact area within 30 seconds, progressing to deep tissue destruction within 5 minutes if not neutralized. The compound can be neutralized by alkaline solution, but the window for effective treatment is narrow.
specifications: spray range: 1-4 meters compound: NecroSolve fast-acting necrotizing enzyme tissue selectivity: Biological only — no effect on synthetics onset: Surface necrosis in 30 seconds deep tissue destruction: 5 minutes if untreated neutralization: Alkaline solution within 2 minutes reservoir: 10 spray bursts weight: 0.8 kg countermeasure: Sealed suit, immediate alkaline flush
story_hooks: A body was found with NecroSolve exposure patterns — the flesh was destroyed but every piece of cyberware was intact and undamaged, neatly arranged as if someone was harvesting augmentations from the living.

Carrion's NecroSolve compound has been detected in a municipal water supply at extremely low concentrations — not enough to cause necrosis, but enough to cause chronic skin inflammation across an entire district.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, brutalist handheld sprayer with a wide nozzle cone and reinforced pressure chamber. The silhouette is deliberately menacing—hunched shoulders with a prominent spray head that resembles a corroded organic mouth. Heavy, industrial aesthetic with zero ergonomic pretense.
physical_description.dimensions: 28cm length, 12cm width at nozzle, 8cm depth. Barrel spray head extends 4cm from main body.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and unbalanced—front-loaded. Feels like holding a pressurized threat. 0.8kg manifests as deliberate mass, not graceful.
physical_description.primary_material: Surgical steel pressure chamber with carbon-reinforced polymer body. Internal surfaces treated to resist NecroSolve corrosion.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with localized surface oxidation—intentionally weathered to suggest chemical exposure. Nozzle cone shows deep pitting and discoloration consistent with acid spray use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with charcoal polymer grip sections. Nozzle cone transitions to sickly bone-white at the aperture. Safety guards in dull biohazard yellow.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubber-polymer hybrid with pronounced ridges. Deliberate texture for wet/gloved operation. Slightly tacky to discourage bare-hand use.
distinctive_features: Wide conical spray nozzle with visible internal ridging—resembles organic aperture
Pressurized gauge window showing fluid level (contents appear cloudy amber/tan)
Manual pump trigger with secondary safety lock requiring two-finger activation
Vent ports along pressure chamber—designed to release thermal buildup from chemical reactions
Corroded manufacturer plate recessed into grip—partially obscured by wear
Faint etching marks on grip where user handles repeatedly
Heat-discolored sections around nozzle—browns and blacks from residual compound contact
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS stamped in raised serif font on left grip panel, heavily oxidized. Serial number laser-etched on chamber, intentionally shallow to suggest field modification. Small biohazard symbol embossed below trigger guard.
physical_description.condition_typical: Severely battle-worn and contaminated. Visible chemical scarring on nozzle and upper body. Organic residue staining around spray aperture despite cleaning attempts. Pressure seals show signs of degradation. Typical field unit shows signs of frequent use and inadequate maintenance—a weapon carried by desperate users.
